<td style="width: 10%;">&#160;</td>
<td style="width: 2%; vertical-align: top;;text-align:left;">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width: 1%; vertical-align: top;">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top;;text-align:left;"> <div style="text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Ford: Invest $29&#160;billion in EVs and autonomous vehicles by 2025 and become carbon neutral by 2050. </div></div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="clear:both;max-height:0pt;"></div> <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Investors </div></div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">Beyond government and corporate action, many investors around the world have increasingly focused on the energy transition as an investment opportunity and have poured record amounts into funds aimed at helping the environment. For example, from January through November 2020, investors in mutual funds and ETFs invested $288&#160;billion globally in sustainable assets, a 96% increase over the whole of 2019, and certain investors have called on companies to disclose a plan for how their business model will be compatible with a <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">net-zero</div> economy. Moreover, EVs have become increasingly popular among consumers, who increased their spending on EVs to $120&#160;billion in 2020, a 50% increase from 2019, according to the International Energy Agency&#8217;s &#8220;Global EV Outlook.&#8221; </div> <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">Total Addressable Market </div></div></div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Thanks to these public and private sector efforts, the global market for EV batteries is anticipated to experience substantial growth characterized by increasing battery pack sizes and decreasing costs. This will be driven by growing EV adoption, as the global number of passenger EVs sold is expected to rise from approximately 2.7&#160;million in 2020 to approximately 90&#160;million in 2040. During this same period, the average battery pack size is projected to increase from 45 kWh / EV to 56 kWh / EV, while the cost of each EV battery pack is anticipated to fall from $150 / kWh to $70 / kWh. The resulting rise in demand for EV batteries is predicted to increase the total addressable market from its 2020 size of approximately $19&#160;billion to an expected approximate $350&#160;billion in 2040. We believe that our superior technology will allow us to play a leading role in this process, while creating value for both our shareholders and society at large. </div></div> <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Our Story </div></div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">Our company was founded in 2012 by Dr.&#160;Qichao Hu through his work in the laboratory of Dr.&#160;Donald Sadoway, an accomplished professor of materials chemistry at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (&#8220;MIT&#8221;). The following year, SES was newly formed based on the work begun at MIT. SES raised a Series A funding round, while Dr.&#160;Hu was named among the 2013 <div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">Forbes</div></div> 30 Under 30 for his work on polymer ionic liquid rechargeable <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> batteries. In 2013, we <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">co-located</div> with A123 Venture Technologies, a technology incubator, to leverage its facility to incubate SES&#8217;s early-stage technology development. SES raised Series B funding in 2015, attracting strategic investors including GM, SAIC Motors and Applied Materials. SES&#8217;s first prototyping battery facility opened in Boston in 2016, while further Series C and C+ funding rounds engaged Temasek and Tianqi in 2017 and SK in 2018, respectively. We capitalized on this momentum, inaugurating our second battery prototyping facility in Shanghai in 2019. </div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">Our company has made strategic advances across several fronts in 2021. SES entered into JDAs with three leading global OEMs - GM, Hyundai and Honda - while simultaneously raising Series D and D+ funding. We also announced our business combination with Ivanhoe Capital Acquisition Corp. With nine years of research and development, we have ambitious plans for the future. With the start of manufacturing by our 1 GWh Pilot Facility and 30 GWh Expansion I Facility approaching, we believe that SES is on the way to becoming a global leader in <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> battery production through our combination of world-class technology and manufacturability at scale. </div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">In 2022, we completed our Business Combination with Old SES, upon which we changed our name to &#8220;SES AI Corporation.&#8221; In connection with the closing of the Business Combination, our shares and warrants started trading on the NYSE under the symbols &#8220;SES&#8221; and &#8220;SES WS,&#8221; respectively. </div></div> <div style="font-size: 8pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-size: 8pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div> <div style="text-align: center; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">59 </div></div> </div> </div> <div style="margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 0em; page-break-before: always;"></div> <hr style="width: 100%; height: 3px; color: rgb(153, 153, 153);"/> <div style="font-size: 13.28px; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div> <div style="text-align: center;"> <div style="width: 8.5in; text-align: left; margin-right: auto; margin-left: auto;"> <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Our Technology </div></div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">We believe that SES <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> is the next generation battery technology for EVs. Our unique approach to <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> is designed to deliver high energy density batteries and high manufacturability at the same time. The unique and differentiated design of our <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> battery, enabled by advanced, proprietary and patented materials and software breakthrough, gives us the confidence that SES will be able to deliver batteries to its customers at scale while matching or exceeding their expectations on performance, safety and cost. </div> <div style="font-size: 12pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-size: 12pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div> <div style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="color: red; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">
<img alt="" src="g297913g84e14.jpg" style="width: 584px; height: 260px;"/></div></div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">Conventional <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-ion</div> technology is currently being used in most commercially available EVs. <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-ion</div> typically uses a metal oxide-based or phosphate-based cathode, and graphite or graphite/silicon-based anodes. The anode and cathode are separated by a polymer-based separator. Finally, the whole cell is filled with a liquid electrolyte that conducts lithium ions from anode to cathode as the vehicle is being driven (or battery is being discharged), and from cathode to anode as the vehicle (or the battery) is being charged. Conventional <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-ion</div> cells have been instrumental in kickstarting the current EV market, and are being manufactured at scale at capacities of hundreds of GWh today. However, the automotive industry and its customers are yearning for a battery with higher energy density to improve the electric driving range (the distance that a vehicle can be driven on a single charge) while reducing battery cost to enable mass-adoption. </div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> is widely considered and accepted as the EV battery technology capable of achieving the highest energy density. In fact, switching the current <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-ion</div> graphite/silicon anode with <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> will currently result in the highest possible energy density for any given cathode in lithium chemistry. Lithium metal is the lightest unengineered pure metal on earth. Also, since the lithium ions do not have to diffuse in and out of the anode host material (like in the case of graphite or silicon in conventional <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-ion),</div> the battery cells made with lithium metal anode can be very compact and light. This combination of lightweight and compact anode results in the highest possible gravimetric (Watt-hour (&#8220;Wh&#8221;)/kg) and volumetric (Wh/liter) energy density, respectively, for any given cathode in lithium chemistry. </div> <div style="font-size: 8pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-size: 8pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div> <div style="text-align: center; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">60 </div></div> </div> </div> <div style="margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 0em; page-break-before: always;"></div> <hr style="width: 100%; height: 3px; color: rgb(153, 153, 153);"/> <div style="font-size: 13.28px; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc" style="text-indent: 0px;">Table of Contents</a></div> <div style="font-size: 13.28px; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc"></a></div> <div style="text-align: center;"> <div style="width: 8.5in; text-align: left; margin-right: auto; margin-left: auto;"> <div style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">
<img alt="" src="g297913g68u75.jpg" style="width: 590px; height: 248px;"/><br/></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">One approach to <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal,</div> known as &#8220;solid-state <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal,&#8221;</div> primarily relies on solid-state materials. The solid-state material refers to the phase (solid) within which lithium ions transport from anode to cathode (during discharge) or cathode to anode (during charge). Conventional <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-ion</div> technology uses liquid electrolytes (not solid electrolytes), and such lithium ion transport is in the liquid phase. Approaches that use solid electrolytes generally suffer from either not having sufficient conductivity at room and lower than room temperatures, poor interface between electrolyte and electrode, inability to suppress lithium dendrites when the solid electrolyte film is thin, and lack of demonstrated manufacturability of thin, large format films and multi-layer cells at scale. </div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">In stark contrast, SES&#8217;s approach to <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> preserves the high energy density benefits of <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> while utilizing a cell design that primarily uses a liquid electrolyte in the cathode and separator to transport the lithium ions. There is also a protective anode coating between the anode and the separator, which consists of solid-state electrolyte materials. Hence, we call our approach <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">&#8220;Li-Metal,&#8221;</div> as it utilizes both liquid and solid electrolyte in the cell simultaneously. This approach results not only in improved energy density due to using lithium metal anode, but also superior performance at room and lower than room temperatures, and enables manufacturing at scale just like <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-ion</div> is manufactured at scale today. In fact, we have been successfully making <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">multi-Ah,</div> multi-layer cells using our <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> approach for many years. In addition to materials, SES&#8217;s <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">AI-powered</div> safety software adds an additional layer of battery health monitoring and safety protection. </div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">The key breakthrough in SES <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> cells is its unique and patented liquid electrolyte. This electrolyte is developed internally at SES with many years of scientific research and development. We use a high-concentration, <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">solvent-in-salt</div></div> electrolyte. SES&#8217;s proprietary liquid electrolyte molecules and formula turns convention on its head. While liquid electrolyte used in conventional <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-ion</div> cells is volatile and flammable, SES liquid electrolyte has low volatility and is self-extinguishing. Conventional liquid electrolytes are primarily made up of organic solvent with low concentration of salt to aid lithium ion conduction. SES liquid electrolyte primarily consists of salt with a very minute amount of proprietary solvent molecule. This new type of high-concentration <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">solvent-in-salt</div></div> liquid electrolyte is fundamentally different from conventional liquid electrolyte. It maintains the manufacturability advantage of liquid electrolyte in conventional <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-ion</div> manufacturing, but can enable <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> due to its stability on lithium metal. </div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">SES&#8217;s proprietary and patented electrolyte helps resolve the issue that has plagued <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> adoption and progress for decades. With repeated charge and discharge cycles, lithium metal anodes are known to develop needle-like mossy structures known as &#8220;dendrites,&#8221; which can penetrate the separator and short-circuit the battery cell. Our electrolyte not only significantly slows down the growth of dendrites, but it also changes its morphology from &#8220;mossy lithium,&#8221; or sharp dendrites, to &#8220;dense deposition,&#8221; or a smooth lithium metal surface. This significantly increases cell cycle life and safety. </div> <div style="font-size: 8pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-size: 8pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div> <div style="text-align: center; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">61 </div></div> </div> </div> <div style="margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 0em; page-break-before: always;"></div> <hr style="width: 100%; height: 3px; color: rgb(153, 153, 153);"/> <div style="font-size: 13.28px; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div> <div style="text-align: center;"> <div style="width: 8.5in; text-align: left; margin-right: auto; margin-left: auto;"> <div style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">
<img alt="" src="g297913g11x83.jpg" style="width: 593px; height: 250px;"/><br/></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">In addition to the electrolyte, our <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> battery cells use a proprietary anode coating that helps provide another layer of protection against dendrites and makes lithium plating denser during charging, as well as advanced <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">AI-powered</div> algorithm to accurately monitor the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">state-of-health</div></div> of the battery cells and detect any impending dendrite-related (or other) safety issues much earlier. </div> <div style="font-size: 12pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-size: 12pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div> <div style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">
<img alt="" src="g297913g49h79.jpg" style="width: 577px; height: 235px;"/><br/></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">The rest of the cell is assembled using our proprietary ultra-thin wide-width lithium metal anode, a conventional <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">state-of-the-art</div></div></div> separator and a cathode. With the exception of the lithium metal anode, all materials and components utilized in our battery cells are either already being manufactured at scale or have the capability to be easily manufactured at scale without the need for intensive research and development, or development of new equipment. </div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">To our knowledge, SES <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metalbattery</div> cells are the only <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> cells demonstrated to meet or exceed the preliminary OEM target requirements for energy density, low temperature discharge, room temperature fast charge and discharge, cycle life and safety. </div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">This unique combination of high-energy density <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> in a hybrid design enables a battery that is expected to be: </div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-size: 6pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div>

<td style="vertical-align: top;;text-align:left;"> <div style="text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; line-height: normal;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">smarter</div></div></div></div>, with <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">AI-powered</div> health monitoring software that can predict safety incidents in real time and make appropriate safety recommendations. </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="clear:both;max-height:0pt;"></div> <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Our Competitive Strengths </div></div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">Differentiated battery technology.</div></div></div></div> As described above, our <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> batteries are expected to be lighter, more energy dense, safer, faster-charging, and lower cost solution than <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-ion</div> batteries, and to include smart technology. Our <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> battery technology has projected energy density of 400 Wh/kg / 1,000 Wh/L (illustrative EV range of approximately 540 miles) in large 100 <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Amp-hour</div> (&#8220;Ah&#8221;) cells, which we believe will help to enable the expansion of an electrified world. Our current 4 Ah multi-layer battery cells have demonstrated energy density of 370 Wh/kg / 700 Wh/L in third-party testing, along with fast charging up to 80% charge in less than 15 minutes, bolstering our confidence in our ability to achieve industry-leading performance. Our batteries are expected to be significantly cheaper in the long-term, while providing fast-charge capabilities, <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">best-in-class</div></div> durability and a high degree of safety. </div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">Designed for manufacturing at scale.</div></div></div></div> Over the last nine years of research and development, we have strived to develop a technology that is not only differentiated, but also scalable and manufacturable. As of September&#160;30, 2021, we had produced more than 15,000 multi-layer <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> battery cells using our <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-ion-like</div></div> production line demonstrating that our batteries are not only playing a leading role in the industry, but are also practical. </div> <div style="font-size: 12pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-size: 12pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div> <div style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">

Leading our business operations are our Founder and Chief Executive Officer Dr.&#160;Qichao Hu, who earned his PhD in Applied Physics from Harvard University and his BS in Physics from MIT, and our President and Chief Operating Officer Rohit Makharia, who previously spent 19 years with GM, 12 of which he spent focusing on fuel cell and battery EVs. Our research, development, engineering and manufacturing efforts are spearheaded by Chief Technology Officer Yongkyu Son, who has 19 years of experience in cell development including with Apple, SK Innovation and SDI, and Chief Science Officer Dr.&#160;Hong Gan, who has 25 years of battery research and development experience in both national labs and industry, during which he made key contributions to silicon based <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-ion</div> and <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-sulfur</div> technologies. font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Our Growth Strategy </div></div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">Our mission is to facilitate the widespread adoption of sustainable electric transportation both on land and in air by creating the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">best-in-class,</div></div> high energy density <div style="white-space: nowrap; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">Battery development for OEMs.</div></div>&#160;The results of tests undertaken by third-party testing facilities under instructions provided by Parent and SES demonstrate industry-leading <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> energy density, performance and safety. We are currently working to develop and produce <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">A-Sample</div> batteries with specifications required by OEMs for their EVs, with the goal of enabling commercial production in 2025. For more information on collaborations with these OEMs, see &#8220;- Our Partnerships&#8221; below. <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">A-Sample</div> batteries are prototypes developed for OEMs based on OEMs&#8217; technical specifications, and they would fully meet those technical specifications. These are in contrast with <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">B-Sample</div> batteries, which would be functional prototypes allowing full drivability and tested in actual vehicles, and <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">C-Sample</div> batteries, which would be fully functional, mature samples for mass production. As we remain focused on <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">A-Sample</div> battery development, we do not yet have any arrangements with OEMs to manufacture consumer-ready batteries for their EVs. </div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">Battery manufacturing at scale. </div></div>We will also continue to enhance our production processes to enable volume manufacturing in a cost-effective manner. We expect to complete our Pilot Facility by 2023, which we expect to be 100% <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">SES-owned</div> and operated. We plan to concurrently develop a 10 GWh joint venture plant that we expect to be operational in 2025 and that will ramp up to 30 GWh by 2027 (our Expansion I Facility), which we expect to be located in the United States. Additionally, we expect to complete a 30 GWh facility in 2026 that will ramp to 70 GWh by 2028 (our Expansion II Facility), which would represent an additional expansion of our existing facilities. In total, we expect to have more than 100 GWh of capacity by 2028. </div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">Partnership development and expansion. </div></div></div></div>As discussed below under &#8220;Our Partnerships,&#8221; while we will continue to strengthen our partnerships with GM, Hyundai and Honda in the use of our battery technology, we intend to work closely with other OEMs to make our <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> battery widely available over time. </div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">Cost reduction.</div></div></div></div> Cost reduction remains an important underpinning of EV market growth and our future growth. Currently, we have no long-term supply arrangements, and expect to negotiate long-term supply contracts as volume grows. For more information, see &#8220;Our Suppliers&#8221; below. However, in addition to arrangements with suppliers, we plan to explore opportunities for partial vertical integration both upstream and downstream. Vertical integration is used by <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-ion</div> battery cell makers to reduce their costs, increase their competitiveness and streamline product development and commercialization for OEMs, by acquiring upstream </div> <div style="font-size: 8pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-size: 8pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div> <div style="text-align: center; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">64 </div></div> </div> </div> <div style="margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 0em; page-break-before: always;"></div> <hr style="width: 100%; height: 3px; color: rgb(153, 153, 153);"/> <div style="font-size: 13.28px; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div> <div style="text-align: center;"> <div style="width: 8.5in; text-align: left; margin-right: auto; margin-left: auto;"> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">and downstream participants in their supply chains. Upstream, we intend to explore integrating vendors of key materials of our cells and providers of key equipment and engineering capabilities, such as cell assembly, anode processing, chemical processing and safety testing. Downstream, we plan to explore integrating providers of key engineering capabilities, such as battery <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">state-of-health</div></div> monitoring software, charging optimization software, battery module development and recycling. </div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">Continued battery innovation. </div></div></div></div>We intend to continue leveraging our world-class science, engineering and manufacturing expertise to innovate future products that will continue to provide leading technology coupled with manufacturability. We continue to invest in research and development in areas such as cell chemistry and structure, battery materials, AI software and advanced manufacturing, to build on our intellectual property portfolio. </div> <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Our Partnerships </div></div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">We intend to work closely with OEMs and other strategic partners to develop and produce our <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> battery cells, with the aim of making them widely available in EVs over time. </div> <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">Existing JDAs </div></div></div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">We have maintained a strong partnership with GM since 2015, when GM led our Series B financing, and since then, GM has invested approximately $70&#160;million in our company, including a $50&#160;million investment in our Series D funding round and a $10&#160;million investment in the PIPE Financing, via GM&#8217;s affiliates and subsidiaries. We plan for our Expansion I Facility to be a joint venture with an OEM strategic partner and that we will supply our own coated anode and electrolyte to the facility, and for our Expansion II Facility to be 100% <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">SES-owned</div> and operated. We expect to use the proceeds from the Business Combination for our Expansion I Facility. We anticipate a combination of debt and equity financing to fund the remaining facilities. Like our current partners and shareholders, we believe that any and all future partners will provide us with important support and resources in developing and scaling our <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> battery technology. </div> <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Our Research and Development </div></div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">We conduct research and development at our facilities in Boston and Shanghai, and expect to eventually build additional facilities in other parts of the world. Research and development activities concentrate on making further improvements to our battery technology, including improvements to battery performance and cost. </div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Our research and development efforts currently include, but are not limited to, programs in the following areas. </div></div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-size: 6pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div>

It attracts and honors employees that want to make a dent in the universe. In addition to competitive compensation and benefits, we set challenging yet meaningful goals for our employees and help them push their limits, as we believe the best and brightest are fundamentally driven by the desire to solve tough, meaningful problems, be part of an exciting movement and make a real impact in the industry. </div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">The health and safety of our employees is paramount at SES. As part of our continuing goal to reduce workplace incidents, we are committed to a culture of safe work practices and improving safety in all of our locations. </div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">We intend to make significant investments in research and development and the recruitment of top technical and engineering talent to improve our battery technology. </div></div> <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Our Facilities </div></div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">Our headquarters are located in Boston, and most of our executive management is located in the United States. Our operating facilities are located in Boston and Shanghai. Both properties are leased, with the Boston lease and the Shanghai lease each expiring in 2026. Our Boston facility focuses on chemistry, materials and algorithm research and development, as well as engaging with OEMs worldwide, including GM, Hyundai and Honda. Our Shanghai facility focuses on supply chain development, manufacturing process development, cell product development, software, BMS and module development. We are building our 1 GWh Pilot Facility in China for the development of <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">pre-commercial-production</div> battery cells, which we expect to be completed in 2023. We have also set up an office in Seoul focused on supply chain, customer relations and our collaboration with partners in the region. As our joint development of <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> batteries with certain U.S. and South Korean OEMs continues to progress, we also expect to launch future research facilities and, eventually, commercial production manufacturing facilities, in the United States and South Korea, while also significantly increasing our headcount in those locations. Specifically, we expect to enter into a joint venture with one or both of our OEM partners to build our Expansion I Facility in the United States. We expect to build the first 10 GWh portion of our Expansion I Facility in the United States in 2023 and 2024, with plans for such facility to be operational by 2025. SES expects that this Expansion I Facility will be located in the United States, as the Expansion I Facility would target the U.S. automotive market (the largest EV market for its OEM partners). </div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">In addition to our 1 GWh Pilot Facility (expected to be built in Shanghai) and our planned 30 GWh and 70 GWh facilities, we are planing to build a pre-production facility in South Korea. We continue to assess our ongoing facilities needs and may build new facilities or lease additional facilities in our current or other locations according to our manufacturing needs and the needs of any OEMs with whom we enter into collaborations. </div></div> <div style="font-size: 12pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-size: 12pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div> <div style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">
<img alt="" src="g297913g80e05.jpg" style="width: 582px; height: 194px;"/><br/></div> <div style="font-size: 8pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-size: 8pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div> <div style="text-align: center; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">68 </div></div> </div> </div> <div style="margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 0em; page-break-before: always;"></div> <hr style="width: 100%; height: 3px; color: rgb(153, 153, 153);"/> <div style="font-size: 13.28px; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div> <div style="text-align: center;"> <div style="width: 8.5in; text-align: left; margin-right: auto; margin-left: auto;"> <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Competition </div></div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">The battery market, like the EV market it services, is fast-growing, extremely competitive and driven by the innovation of both large incumbents and emerging entrants like SES. CATL, SKI, LGES, Panasonic and SDI are among the existing suppliers of batteries to the EV industry. Although their offerings tend to be conventional <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-ion,</div> they could develop <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> batteries that would directly compete with our offerings. Additionally, the efforts of OEMs, including Tesla, Nio, Rivian and Toyota, to develop their own EV battery production capabilities could reduce demand for SES&#8217;s technology if they are successful. Newer entrants, including Northvolt, Sila Nanotechnologies, Solid Power, QuantumScape, Ganfeng Lithium and WeLion, are supplying next-generation batteries that could compete with ours, and others could feasibly emerge. </div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">We acknowledge that incumbents and emerging entrants may have greater resources to invest in advancing their technologies, access to more potential customers, or strategic relationships with OEMs (or other third parties) that may give them a competitive edge. We further acknowledge that these disparities, where they exist, have the potential to harm our business, results of operations or financial condition. However, SES combines the technology innovation of emerging entrants with the practical execution capability of incumbents, and we believe that SES, with its determination and focus, will be able to be successful in the competitive <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Li-Metal</div> space. </div> <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Government Regulation and Compliance </div></div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">There are government regulations pertaining to battery safety, transportation of batteries, use of batteries in vehicles, factory safety and disposal of hazardous materials. We will ultimately have to comply with these regulations to sell our batteries into the market. For more information, see &#8220;Risk Factors - Risks Relating to SES&#8217;s Business and Industry - Risks Relating to Regulation and Legal Compliance&#8221; discussing regulations and regulatory risks related to export controls (including our export controls compliance program), environmental, health and safety, anti-corruption, anti-bribery, data collection, trade and tax law compliance. </div></div> <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Legal Proceedings </div></div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">From time to time, we may become involved in litigation or other legal proceedings. We are not currently a party to any litigation or legal proceedings that, in the opinion of our management, are likely to have a material adverse effect on our business. Regardless of outcome, litigation can have an adverse impact on us because of defense and settlement costs, diversion of management resources and other factors. </div></div> <div style="font-size: 8pt; Additionally, we expect to complete a 30 GWh facility in 2026 that will ramp to 70 GWh by 2028 (our Expansion II Facility), which would represent an additional expansion of our existing facilities. In total, we expect to have more than 100 GWh of capacity by 2028. </div> <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">Competition </div></div></div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">The battery market, like the EV market it services, is fast-growing, extremely competitive and driven by the innovation of both large incumbents and emerging entrants like SES. We acknowledge that the incumbents and other emerging entrants may have greater resources to invest in advancing their technologies, access to more potential customers, or strategic relationships with OEMs (or other third parties) that may give them a competitive edge. Since that point, the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">COVID-19</div> pandemic has caused general business disruption throughout the United States and worldwide. The effects and potential effects of <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">COVID-19,</div> include, but are not limited to, its impact on general economic conditions, trade and financing markets, changes in customer behavior and has created significant uncertainty in the overall continuity in business operations. The spread of <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">COVID-19</div> has also disrupted the manufacturing, delivery and overall supply chain of EV manufacturers and suppliers and EV batteries, and has led to a global decrease in vehicle sales in markets around the world. In particular, the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">COVID-19</div> crisis may cause a decrease in demand for EV batteries if fleet operators delay purchases of vehicles or if fuel prices for internal combustion engine vehicles remain at levels that do not create an incentive to accelerate the migration from internal combustion engine vehicles to EVs, an increase in costs resulting from efforts of manufacturers of EVs or EV batteries to mitigate the effects of <div style="white-space: nowrap; As a precaution, we took certain preventive measures in light of this pandemic and reduced our operational activities during the year ended December&#160;31, 2020. In particular, we temporarily reduced employee compensation, recommended that all <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">non-essential</div> personnel work from home, and reduce <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">in-person</div> participation in research and development activities. We also were required to implement additional safety protocols for essential workers, which resulted in delays in the timing of project execution. </div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">Following the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">re-opening</div> of <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">non-essential</div> businesses and the easing of restrictions on <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">non-essential</div> <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">in-person</div> work, since January&#160;1, 2021, we have ramped up research and development hiring and increased our investment in <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">in-person</div> work. letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">Research and Development </div></div></div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Research and development expenses consist primarily of costs incurred for salaries and personnel-related expenses, including stock-based compensation expense, for scientists, experienced engineers and technicians including the material and supplies used in product research and development, process engineering efforts and testing, as well as payments to consultants, patent related legal costs, depreciation, and allocated facilities and information technology costs. As we attempt to develop a battery cell with acceptable performance, yields and costs, we anticipate that research and development and related expenses will increase significantly for the foreseeable future as a result of additional hiring of scientists, engineers and technicians and investment in additional plant and equipment for product development, building prototypes and testing of battery cells. </div></div> <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">General and Administrative </div></div></div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">General and administrative expenses consist primarily of costs incurred for salaries and personnel-related expenses, including stock-based compensation expense, for our finance, legal and human resource functions, expenses for director and officer insurance, outside contractor and professional service fees, audit and compliance expenses, legal, accounting and other advisory services, as well as allocated facilities and information technology costs including depreciation. We are rapidly expanding our personnel headcount, in anticipation of planning for and supporting our growth and operating as a public company. Accordingly, we expect our general and administrative expenses to increase significantly in the near term and for the foreseeable future. </div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Upon commencement of commercial operations, we also expect to incur customer and sales support and advertising costs. </div></div> <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">Interest income </div></div></div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Interest income primarily consists of interest earned on our cash and cash equivalents, which are primarily invested in money market funds and interest income from short-term investments, which are primarily invested in corporate bonds and mutual funds. </div></div> <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">Other (expense) income, net </div></div></div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Other (expense) income, net consists primarily of foreign exchange gains or losses and forgiveness of the unsecured note payable under Paycheck Protection Program (&#8220;PPP&#8221;) established pursuant to the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act (the &#8220;CARES Act&#8221;) and administered by the U.S. Small Business Administration (&#8220;SBA&#8221;). </div></div> <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">Provision for Income Taxes </div></div></div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Provision for income taxes consists of an estimate for state and foreign income taxes based on enacted rates, as adjusted for allowable credits, deductions, uncertain tax positions, changes in deferred tax assets and liabilities, and changes in the tax law. We maintain a full valuation allowance against our net deferred tax assets because we believe it is more likely than not that these deferred tax assets will not be realized. </div></div> <div style="font-size: 8pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-size: 8pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div> <div style="text-align: center; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; <td style="vertical-align: top;;text-align:left;"> <div style="text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">&#8220;nm&#8221; means not meaningful. </div></div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="clear:both;max-height:0pt;"></div> <div style="font-size: 8pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-size: 8pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div> <div style="text-align: center; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">75 </div></div> </div> </div> <div style="margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 0em; page-break-before: always;"></div> <hr style="width: 100%; height: 3px; color: rgb(153, 153, 153);"/> <div style="font-size: 13.28px; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div> <div style="text-align: center;"> <div style="width: 8.5in; text-align: left; margin-right: auto; margin-left: auto;"> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Operating Expenses: Research and Development </div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">Research and development expenses increased $1.5&#160;million, or 66%, to $3.7&#160;million for the three months ended September&#160;30, 2021, from $2.2&#160;million for the three months ended September&#160;30, 2020. The increase primarily resulted from the $1.1&#160;million increase in personnel cost mainly attributable to our growth in headcount in support of our ongoing research and development efforts of battery cell development, following the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">re-opening</div> of <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">non-essential</div> businesses and the easing of restrictions on <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">non-essential</div> <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">in-person</div> work stemming from the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">COVID-19</div> pandemic and $0.6&#160;million increase in expenses for lab consumables and material supplies related to our increased research and development activities during the three months ended September&#160;30, 2021. An additional driver was a $0.3&#160;million increase in professional fees, outside services, facility and office expenses related to our ongoing research and development activities for the three months ended September&#160;30, 2021. </div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">Research and development expenses increased $2.9&#160;million, or 40%, to $10.2&#160;million for the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2021, from $7.3&#160;million for the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2020. The increase primarily resulted from the $1.9&#160;million increase in personnel cost mainly attributable to our growth in headcount in support of our ongoing research and development efforts, following the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">re-opening</div> of <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">non-essential</div> businesses and the easing of restrictions on <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">non-essential</div> <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">in-person</div> work stemming from the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">COVID-19</div> pandemic during the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2021. An additional driver was a $1.0&#160;million increase in professional fees, expenses for lab consumables and material supplies related to our increased research and development activities, outside services, facility and office expenses related to our ongoing research and development activities for the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2021. </div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Operating Expenses: General and Administrative </div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">General and administrative expenses increased $3.3&#160;million, or 318%, to $4.4&#160;million for the three months ended September&#160;30, 2021, from $1.0&#160;million for the three months ended September&#160;30, 2020. The increase in general and administrative expenses primarily resulted from a $1.7&#160;million increase in professional fees associated with external consulting, legal and accounting services, a $0.9&#160;million increase in marketing and public relations expense, and a $0.5&#160;million increase attributable to our growth in headcount in preparation for operating as a public company. Furthermore, there was $0.2&#160;million increase in outside services, facility and office expenses during the three months ended September&#160;30, 2021. </div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">General and administrative expenses increased $6.1&#160;million, or 214%, to $8.9&#160;million for the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2021, from $2.8&#160;million for the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2020. The increase in general and administrative expenses primarily resulted from a $3.8&#160;million increase in professional fees associated with external legal, consulting and accounting services, a $1.3&#160;million increase in marketing and public relations activity, and a $1.0&#160;million increase attributable to our growth in headcount in preparation for operating as a public company. </div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Interest Income </div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Interest income for the three months ended September&#160;30, 2021 increased $0.2&#160;million due to a short-term investment made during the second quarter of 2021 from the proceeds of Series D and D plus financing. Interest income for the three months ended September&#160;30, 2020 was immaterial. </div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Interest income increased $0.1&#160;million, or 130%, to $0.2&#160;million for the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2021, from $0.1&#160;million for the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2020. The increase in interest income was attributable to a short-term investment made during the second quarter of 2021 from the proceeds of Series D and D plus financing. </div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Other (expense) income, net </div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Other (expense) income, net increased $47,000, or 100%, to $94,000 for the three months ended September&#160;30, 2021, from $47,000 for the three months ended September&#160;30, 2020. The increase was mainly attributable to foreign exchange loss. </div></div> <div style="font-size: 8pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-size: 8pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div> <div style="text-align: center; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">76 </div></div> </div> </div> <div style="margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 0em; page-break-before: always;"></div> <hr style="width: 100%; height: 3px; color: rgb(153, 153, 153);"/> <div style="font-size: 13.28px; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div> <div style="text-align: center;"> <div style="width: 8.5in; text-align: left; margin-right: auto; margin-left: auto;"> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Other (expense) income, net increased to $0.7&#160;million for the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2021, which resulted from an $0.8&#160;million gain recorded as a result of forgiveness of the loan received in 2020 under the PPP established pursuant to the CARES Act. Other (expense) income, net for the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2020 was immaterial. </div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">Provision for Income Taxes </div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">The provision for income tax expense during the three and nine months ended September&#160;30, 2021 and 2020 were immaterial. The effective tax rate was (0.04)% and 0% for the three months ended September&#160;30, 2021 and 2020, respectively. The effective tax rate was (0.12)% and 0% for the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2021 and 2020, respectively. The difference between the provision for income taxes and the income tax determined by applying the statutory federal income tax rate of 21% principally results from losses generated in the U.S. where no benefit was recorded because the Company had fully reserved its deferred tax assets as of September&#160;30, 2021 and December&#160;31, 2020 and the recording of uncertain tax positions and interest expense. </div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">The Company&#8217;s deferred tax assets principally result from U.S. net operating loss carryforwards and research credits. Utilization of these attributes is dependent upon future levels of taxable income and may be subject to annual limitation due to the &#8220;change in ownership provisions&#8221; under Section&#160;382 of the Internal Revenue Code. Such limitations may result in the expiration of these attributes before their utilization. The Company is evaluating the impact of the equity transactions that have occurred during the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2021, however it does not believe there will be a material impact to the attributes. During the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2021, there were no significant changes to the total amount of unrecognized tax benefits. </div></div> <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 18pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">Comparison of the Year Ended December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019 </div></div></div></div> <div style="text-indent: 4%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">The following table sets forth our historical operating results for the periods indicated (amounts in thousands): </div></div> <div style="font-size: 12pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-size: 12pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div>
